original_title: Xbox's Confusing Exclusivity Criteria Now Aided by 'EXCLUSIVE' Label on Console Dashboard
summary_en: Xbox is introducing a new 'EXCLUSIVE' label on its console dashboard to clearly denote which games will be playable only on Xbox consoles. This move aims to clear up confusion around Microsoft's evolving approach to game exclusivity.
ai_analysis: This label signifies a tangible step towards transparency in Xbox's exclusivity strategy, which has been a point of discussion for fans navigating platform choices.

en.title: Xbox Adds 'EXCLUSIVE' Label to Dashboard, Clarifying Console Game Strategy
en.summary: Xbox is introducing a new 'EXCLUSIVE' label on its console dashboard to clearly denote which games will be playable only on Xbox consoles. This move aims to clear up confusion around Microsoft's evolving approach to game exclusivity.
en.body:
Xbox has rolled out a new 'EXCLUSIVE' label on its console dashboard, a move designed to bring much-needed clarity to its often-debated exclusivity strategy. This visual cue aims to help players quickly identify titles that will be console-exclusive to the Xbox ecosystem, distinguishing them from games that might also land on PC or remain multiplatform.

The label has already begun appearing, notably for upcoming titles like **Gears of War: E-Day** and **Clockwork Revolution**. **Gears of War: E-Day**, slated for an October 6 release, is now clearly marked as a console exclusive, a designation that also applies to **Clockwork Revolution** when it launches in 2027. While both these titles will still be available on PC, the 'EXCLUSIVE' tag on the console dashboard specifically signals their absence from competing platforms like PlayStation.

This initiative comes as Xbox's Chief Content Officer, **Matt Booty**, has emphasized a nuanced approach to exclusivity. He previously stated that decisions would be made on a "case-by-case basis," with a commitment to keeping "big multiplayer games and live-service games" multiplatform. The new label provides a concrete way for players to understand these distinctions directly within the console interface.

## Clearing the Console Air

For years, the definition of an "Xbox exclusive" has been a shifting target. With acquisitions like Bethesda and Activision Blizzard, and the rise of Game Pass, the lines between console-exclusive, PC-available, and truly multiplatform releases have often blurred. This new label is a direct response to player feedback and the need for a more transparent system. It helps Xbox fans feel confident about what they can expect to play only on their chosen platform, reinforcing the value proposition of owning an Xbox console.

> "We want a reason for people to get on board with Xbox, we want them to have a reason to buy an Xbox, we want them to have a reason to be an Xbox fan. At the same time, we want to reward all our players that have been with us for a long time — we know that exclusives are important, and that's why we've got Gears coming in 2026 and Clockwork [Revolution] coming in 2027." — **Matt Booty**

## What This Means for Gamers

This label is more than just a cosmetic addition; it's a tool for players making purchasing decisions. In a landscape where cross-play and cross-progression are increasingly common, knowing which games are truly locked to a specific console ecosystem is crucial. For dedicated Xbox fans, it provides reassurance that Microsoft is still investing in platform-defining experiences. For those on the fence, it offers a clearer picture of what the Xbox ecosystem uniquely offers.

While the 'EXCLUSIVE' tag is currently visible on the console dashboard, its absence from the Xbox.com store pages for these titles suggests a phased rollout. Players can expect this clarity to extend across more of Xbox's digital storefronts as the company continues to refine its communication strategy.

## What's Next

The upcoming months will reveal how consistently this 'EXCLUSIVE' label is applied across all relevant Xbox titles. Fans will be watching closely to see if it becomes a standard feature for all console-exclusive releases, providing a definitive guide to platform availability.

content_raw: Xbox has rolled out a new label for console exclusive games, visible now on your Xbox Series X/S dashboard. This month, Xbox confirmed it had decided to make the upcoming Gears of War: E-Day a console exclusive when it arrives on October 6. Clockwork Revolution will also be a console exclusive when it launches in 2027. Now, Gears of War: E-Day features a brand new "EXCLUSIVE" label, similar to other previous game labels that denote a game is optimized for Series X/S, or featured as part of a subscription service such as Game Pass or Ubisoft+. The label certainly makes clear the game will no longer be arriving for PlayStation 5 (as had once been planned), though it's worth remembering that the title will still also launch on PC. Still, the label will likely prove useful helping mark out the titles that Microsoft has decided it will make exclusive — something chief content officer Matt Booty has said will be chosen on a "case-by-case basis" , but not include "big multiplayer games and live-service games," which will remain multiplatform. There's no sign yet of a similar label on the game's Xbox.com store page (or the one for Clockwork Revolution), but with its launch still not for several months, there's still time. "We want a reason for people to get on board with Xbox, we want them to have a reason to buy an Xbox, we want them to have a reason to be an Xbox fan," Booty said previously. "At the same time, we want to reward all our players that have been with us for a long time — we know that exclusives are important, and that's why we've got Gears coming in 2026 and Clockwork [Revolution] coming in 2027." "We also want to be clear that our big multiplayer games and live-service games are going to continue to be multiplatform," he continued. "If we've promised something to players already, we're going to honor that promise. And then — I think Asha said it — we're going to make the right decision and not the fast decision. "We're going to keep thinking about this going forward," Booty concluded, "and, I think you guys know already, our principle is when we announce the date, we announce the platforms. So, it's going to be case-by-case, but we're going to be clear, that when it's got a date, it's got a platform and you'll know what the choice is going to be." This approach has been dubbed as confusing by some fans, and feels like it will take a while to settle down. As newly-installed Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said, the company will firstly honor all previously-announced games coming to PlayStation (including Halo: Campaign Evolved, for example) and look to make more unannounced games exclusive if and when the company's finances improve. In other words, for now, expect more announcements of new Xbox titles where PlayStation 5 and even Nintendo Switch 2 versions are confirmed as well. This was the case just this month, when Xbox made State of Decay 3's PlayStation 5 version made official , Hellblade threequel Senua was unveiled and confirmed for PS5 ,
